Thanks again for the demo — Evergreen’s security team asked me to follow up with a couple of specific asks before we share Redwood with our dev teams. Quick list: 

- Can you provide a single-file subprocessor inventory (current snapshot) and a short plain-language blurb we can paste in our vendor register? Our auditors prefer a very concise explanation (1-2 lines) of what each subprocessor does.
- Under the DPA, we saw a clause about cross-border transfers. Can you confirm which mechanisms you rely on for transfers (SCCs/UK Addendum, standard contractual clauses, adequacy, or other) for Hosted API customers? A one-paragraph explanation is fine.
- Related: is there a shorter customer-facing FAQ we can include in the vendor entry that explains data residency options and whether customer data is retained for billing/analytics?

If it helps, Rodrigo is our procurement lead and will coordinate on formal DPA redlines later in the week. Could you send those artifacts as separate attachments? Ideally a CSV for the subprocessor list and a 1-page plain-language summary of the DPA items.

Appreciate it — we’re trying to get this into our procurement queue by Friday.

Cheers,

Thanks for the tag. Short answers for Emily and Evergreen: 

- Transfers: For Hosted API customers that do not elect private deployment or data residency controls, we rely primarily on EU/UK Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) where applicable and, for certain partners in APAC, contractual safeguards plus documented access controls. We also offer dedicated-region Hosted plans where data is stored and processed within the chosen region (US/EU) — that is noted in the product FAQ.

- Retention for billing/analytics: We retain aggregated usage metrics for billing and product analytics. Customer-level request/response data used for debugging or support is ephemeral by default and is only retained with explicit customer consent or under a support ticket; see the DPA section on data handling.

- Redlines: We prefer limited edits to standard DPA terms; major deviations (e.g., on indemnities or data residency guarantees) will need legal review. I’ll attach a short 1-page plain-language summary that addresses the above.

Please flag any specific regulatory requirements (HIPAA/BAA needs, etc.) — Evergreen, if you need a BAA we can route through our enterprise security process.

Marissa Cole
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
